api:
<BarGauge> shows one or more values as bars filled between a minimum and a maximum, coloured by thresholds or a colour scheme. If you have used Grafana's Bar Gauge panel, see Coming from Grafana.

Display options

PropEffect
displayGradient fills the bar with a blend of the colours it passes through. Lcd lights up separate cells. Basic is a flat bar with a solid edge.
orientationHorizontal stacks the bars as rows. Vertical lays them out as columns. Auto picks columns when the area is wider than it is tall.
name_placementTop puts the name above the bar, Left beside it, Hidden hides it. Auto places it on top when the row is taller than 40px, otherwise on the left. Vertical bars always show the name underneath.
text_modeValue, Name, ValueAndName or None. Auto shows the name when there's more than one bar or you provide a name accessor.
value_modeColor draws the value in the bar's colour, Text in the normal text colour, Hidden hides it.
show_unfilledDraws the empty part of the track. Ignored in Lcd mode.
sizingAuto divides the space evenly, with rows between 16 and 300px tall and columns at least 8px wide. Sizing::Manual { min_width, min_height, max_height } sets those limits yourself.
title_size, value_sizeFixed text sizes instead of sizes fitted to the space.

When the bars need more room than the area has, the ones that don't fit are cut off.

Range, colour and thresholds

The bar's length is its value's position between min and max. Values above max fill the bar, and values below min or missing (NaN) show only a sliver.

GaugeColor
VariantColour of each bar
GaugeColor::Thresholdsthe threshold step the value has reached
GaugeColor::Palettethe next colour from your theme's palette, one per bar
GaugeColor::Scheme(Scheme)the value's position between min and max on a colour scheme
GaugeColor::Fixed(Hsla)one colour for every bar

In Gradient mode, thresholds and schemes also blend along the bar: with thresholds the bar passes through each step it has reached, and with a scheme it shows the whole scheme along the track. In Lcd mode, each cell takes the colour for its own position.

Thresholds
static STEPS: LazyLock<[(f64, Hsla); 3]> =
    LazyLock::new(|| [(f64::NEG_INFINITY, rgb(0x40a02b)), (60., rgb(0xdf8e1d)), (85., rgb(0xd20f39))]);

thresholds={Thresholds::absolute(&STEPS[..])}
ConstructorStep values are
Thresholds::absolute(steps)values in the same units as the data
Thresholds::percentage(steps)percentages of the min–max range, from 0 to 100

The first step is the base colour, used for everything below the second step, so its value doesn't matter. Each later step applies from its value upwards. Steps take a Vec or a &'static slice; a static slice costs nothing to rebuild on every render.

Value text

The value is shown using format if you set it, otherwise with decimals, otherwise with up to three decimals and the trailing zeros dropped.

format={|v| format!("{v:.0} GiB").into()}

examples.title: Disk usage
examples.description: One bar per row, gradient through the default thresholds.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn disk_usage() {
    let data = use_signal(disks());
    rsx! {
        <BarGauge data={data} name={|d: &Disk| d.mount} value={|d| d.used} class="h-64" />
    }
}

examples.title: Reduce a frame
examples.description: One bar per field, showing its last value.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn reduce_a_frame() {
    let frame = use_signal(services());
    rsx! {
        <BarGauge data={frame} reduce={Reduce::Calc(Calc::Last)} max={400.} class="h-64" />
    }
}

examples.title: Pick fields
examples.description: Only some fields, reduced to their mean.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn pick_fields() {
    let frame = use_signal(services());
    rsx! {
        <BarGauge
            data={frame}
            reduce={Reduce::Calc(Calc::Mean)}
            fields={&["api", "worker"]}
            max={300.}
            display={BarDisplay::Basic}
            class="h-64"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Percentage thresholds
examples.description: Your own steps, as a percentage of the range.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn custom_thresholds() {
    let data = use_signal(disks());
    rsx! {
        <BarGauge
            data={data}
            name={|d: &Disk| d.mount}
            value={|d| d.used}
            thresholds={Thresholds::percentage(&STEPS[..])}
            class="h-64"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Units and range
examples.description: Custom range and value text, no unfilled track.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn units_and_range() {
    let data = use_signal(disks());
    rsx! {
        <BarGauge
            data={data}
            name={|d: &Disk| d.mount}
            value={|d| d.used * 10.24}
            min={0.}
            max={1024.}
            format={|v| format!("{v:.0} GiB").into()}
            show_unfilled={false}
            color={GaugeColor::Fixed(rgb(0x1e66f5))}
            class="h-64"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Live data
examples.description: A signal as data: bars move when it changes.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live_value() {
    let data = use_signal(disks());
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-64">
            <div class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline" onClick={move || data.update(|rows| rows.iter_mut().for_each(|d| d.used = (d.used * 1.37) % 100.))}>
                "Shuffle"
            </div>
            <BarGauge data={data} name={|d: &Disk| d.mount} value={|d| d.used} class="flex-1" />
        </div>
    }
}
